messages.author: 12a8430c1bf3f70b
messages.subject: ggExtra - arrange()
parts:
Good afternoon,

I'm only new to ggplot2... and I'm not sure what to do to start over...

require(ggplot2)
require(ggExtra)

plots = lapply(1:5, function(.x) qplot(1:10,rnorm(10),main=paste("plot",.x)))
arrange(plots[[1]],plots[[2]], tableGrob(head(iris)), plots[[3]],
nrow=2, as.table=TRUE, main="test main", sub=textGrob("test sub",
gp=gpar(font=2)))

# NEW PLOT : I want to start again?
arrange(plots[[4]],plots[[3]], tableGrob(head(iris)), plots[[2]],
nrow=2, as.table=TRUE, main="Over WRITING old main",
sub=textGrob("MORE OVER-WRITING", gp=gpar(font=2)))

without saying dev.off() how do I cleanly say I want to start a new
plot at "# NEW PLOT : I want to start again?" ?

Thanks in advance,
Sean

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: ggExtra - arrange()
parts:
Hi,

grid.newpage() should do it. Please note that arrange() is actually
part of the gridExtra package, a dependency of ggExtra, and that
neither (experimental) package is supported by this ggplot2 list.

HTH,

baptiste

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: ggExtra - arrange()
parts:
Hi,

If you look at the source code for arrange() you'll see that it's
basically a wrapper around the grid.layout arrangements of Hadley's
book. As far as this function is concerned it's fairly reliable and
stable; the "experimental" part I was referring to was more related to
other functions (e.g. new ggplot geoms, etc.). Feel free to drop me a
line offlist with possible enhancements for arrange() if you do find
it useful.

Best,

baptiste
